title: Quinoa and Roasted Vegetable Salad
subtitle: Fluffy quinoa with roasted courgette, pepper and spinach
excerpt: Quinoa tossed with roasted courgette, red pepper and spinach, dressed in lemon juice and olive oil. A high-protein grain salad that eats as a full lunch and keeps well in the fridge.
sourceNotes: Quinoa moved from specialist health-food ingredient to mainstream supermarket staple in Britain around 2010, following its growth as a health food in the United States. Its combination with roasted vegetables became a standard of the contemporary British lunch repertoire. Quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa) is a South American grain-like seed domesticated in the Andean region; it provides a complete protein, which made it attractive to the health-food market.

recipe.batchNotes: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Roast vegetables and cook quinoa ahead; assemble before serving.

content.text: Quinoa absorbs dressing well and keeps its texture for days in the fridge, which makes it practical for batch cooking. Rinse the quinoa before cooking to remove the bitter outer coating (saponins). Use a 2-to-1 ratio of water to grain and a lid on the pan; the quinoa is done when the liquid is absorbed and the white germ ring has separated from the seed.
Heat the oven to 200 C. Toss the courgette and red pepper with 3 tablespoons of olive oil and 0.5 tsp of salt on a baking tray. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until tender and coloured.

Put {{quinoa}} of rinsed quinoa in a saucepan with 400 ml of cold water and a pinch of salt. Bring to the boil, reduce the heat to low, cover and cook for 12 to 15 minutes until the water is absorbed. Remove from the heat and leave covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Tip the warm quinoa into a large bowl. Add the roasted vegetables and spinach and toss; the residual heat will wilt the spinach slightly. Drizzle over the lemon juice and 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Season with salt and {{black-pepper}} of black pepper. Toss and serve.

items.fix: Rinse thoroughly in a fine-mesh sieve under cold running water for at least 30 seconds before cooking.
Use a 2-to-1 ratio of water to quinoa. Remove from the heat as soon as the water is absorbed and the germ rings are visible. Do not stir during cooking.

content.text: Quinoa salad arrived in British home cooking via health cafes and deli counters in the 2000s. It became popular for its protein content, light texture and ability to sit in the fridge without going soggy. It works as a packed lunch, a dinner-party side or a buffet dish.
